title: Vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC)
what: This is a vaginal birth for a woman who had a cesarean section before. It is done under close watch by doctors.
why: When the scar on the uterus from the cesarean is strong and there are no other reasons for surgery. The decision is made together with your doctor.
duration: labor length varies, usually many hours; the hospital stay is usually 2 to 4 days
tell_doctor: Why you had your last cesarean
If there were problems after that surgery

prepare.title: Consultation
prepare.text: Talk with your doctor ahead of time about whether you can give birth vaginally and what the risks are.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Bring the discharge notes from your last surgery. They are very important.

prepare.title: Hospital
prepare.text: Usually you choose a maternity hospital where emergency surgery can be done at any time of day.

prepare.title: Bag
prepare.text: Pack your hospital bag ahead of time.

bring: Discharge notes from your last cesarean
steps: When contractions start or your waters break, you go to the maternity hospital
The doctor examines you and does an ultrasound of the scar if needed
Your baby's heartbeat is usually recorded all the time
An IV line is placed in your vein just in case
Contractions go as in a regular birth, and pain relief is possible
If something goes wrong, the doctors may switch to a cesarean
Your baby is placed on your chest
feel: Contractions are painful, as in a regular birth. Discuss pain relief with your doctor
The monitor belt on your belly can make it harder to move
after: Recovery is usually faster than after a cesarean
Bleeding and how you feel are checked in the hospital
A doctor's visit after discharge. You will be told when
red_flags: Sudden pain at the scar: tell the staff right away
Bleeding after you go home: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C or severe belly pain

faq.q: Is it safe to give birth vaginally after a cesarean?
faq.a: For many women, yes. But the doctor decides after an exam and a review of your last surgery.

faq.q: What if it does not work?
faq.a: Then the doctors will do a cesarean. That is why the birth takes place where this can be done quickly.

reminders.text: Your due date is close. Check your hospital bag, your pregnancy record, and the notes from your last cesarean.
